quote: Eternity is in love with the productions of time.
source: William Blake, The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, Proverbs of Hell, the tenth proverb (1790)

evidence.where: Wikisource transcription of The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (copy D) read in full, and the Project Gutenberg text of the work; both print the proverb in this wording and both place it tenth in the sequence, after He whose face gives no light, shall never become a star and before The busy bee has no time for sorrow.
evidence.edition: Wikisource transcription following copy D (1793); Project Gutenberg ebook 45315
evidence.locator: Proverbs of Hell, tenth proverb (plate 7 in the Erdman and Bentley plate numbering; facsimile editions number the plate differently, so the locator counts proverbs instead)

reason: The line is Blake's own, in the named work, in this exact wording with its terminal stop, and it stands tenth in the Proverbs of Hell as the proposal states. Blake is unshipped, unbanned and at zero for the year, and the proverb counts what a day makes rather than consoling, which suits a month on truth and clarity.
